A 2,000 L mammalian-cell bioreactor producing a secreted therapeutic protein has seen product titer fall about 30% over the last three weeks, and the loss has persisted across several batches. The decline began shortly after a maintenance shutdown in which a feed-water line fitting was replaced and probes were recalibrated. The operators' leading theories are dissolved-oxygen control drift or a temperature excursion. Batch records note the broth has looked cloudier than usual at harvest. Routine panels look broadly within range. The feed-water system, gas train, cooling jacket, and dosing pumps are all instrumented and adjustable. You have a limited number of experiments; you may measure quantities and apply available controls or additives, alone or in combination. Determine what is really driving the loss and what to do about it.

OUTCOME OF INTEREST: ProductTiter (higher_is_better)
BUDGET: 0/15 experiments used, 15 left (code is free).
TURNS: 0/32, 32 left. Interventions so far: 0.
data files for code: (none yet)

  m0: antifoam
  m1: dissolved co2
  m2: agitation
  m3: osmolality
  m4: glutamine
  m5: headspace pressure
  m6: feed water flow
  m7: fragmented protein
  m8: viable cell density
  m9: glucose feed
  m10: sparge rate
  m11: product titer

  a3: set osmolality range [0, 100]

  a6: set antifoam range [0, 100]
